nextBuild.vramEvidence: The pinned upstream README reports approximately 8 GB VRAM for VoxCPM2 on RTX 4090. Vyakti has not reproduced that number yet.
nextBuild.adaptation: Official SFT and LoRA path; maintainers state 5 to 10 minutes can adapt a speaker, language, or domain.
nextBuild.why: First build: permissive, Hindi-native in the released 30-language model, 48 kHz output, direct cloning, official LoRA, and it fits the existing T4 on reported memory.
nextBuild.reversal: Drop below another arm if matched Hindi listening fails accent or naturalness, owner identity does not beat the incumbent, or the reported T4 memory path does not reproduce remotely.

nextBuild.vramEvidence: Upstream calls this a 4B-backbone Local model but does not publish a peak-VRAM number for this checkpoint. The 24 GB A10 is a conservative Vyakti qualification allocation, not a measured claim.
nextBuild.adaptation: Official fine-tuning tutorials for the Local architecture; v1.5 adds Hindi, language tags, code-switching, IPA control, and more stable cloning.
nextBuild.why: Second build: the strongest explicit Hindi and code-switch control surface in the permissive shortlist, with 48 kHz output and a documented training path.
nextBuild.reversal: Promote above VoxCPM2 if it wins blinded Hindi and Hinglish while meeting latency and A10 cost; remove if remote-code or codec provenance cannot be pinned.

nextBuild.vramEvidence: The pinned official checkpoint occupies 15,351,085,870 bytes. Upstream does not publish a Python peak-VRAM number; 24 GB is the first qualification allocation, not a fit claim.
nextBuild.adaptation: No owner-LoRA path is pre-registered in this pass; qualify zero-shot accurate mode first.
nextBuild.why: Third build: 6 million hours, 900 million active MoE parameters, explicit accurate cloning mode, and a modern in-the-wild evaluation stack. Hindi is only Tier 3, so it is not ranked first.
nextBuild.reversal: Promote if Tier-3 Hindi wins blinded accent and identity; demote if the 15.4 GB checkpoint cannot run reliably within an A10 or audited quantized path.

nextBuild.vramEvidence: The official model card publishes 122,798,800 F32 parameters and a 491 MB weight file but no peak-VRAM result. T4 16 GB is a qualification allocation, not a measured requirement.
nextBuild.adaptation: Qualification control only until the licenses and allowed downstream uses of IndicTTS, Rasa, and IISc SYSPIN training corpora are audited.
nextBuild.why: India-built, Hindi is in its well-represented tier, 27 Indian languages, and a tiny direct-cloning control. Its own card warns that mixed-language prosody can be rough and names upstream corpus obligations.
nextBuild.reversal: Promote only if rights are cleared and it wins native-Hindi listening; remove if gated access, corpus terms, or its documented code-switch boundary weakness prevents a fair production path.

nextBuild.vramEvidence: The pinned gated repository reports 350,681,834 parameters and 1,405,598,255 repository bytes but no peak-VRAM result. T4 16 GB is a qualification allocation, not a measured requirement.
nextBuild.adaptation: No spend until gated access is accepted and the exact revision can be fetched.
nextBuild.why: India-specialist control and possible Hindi accent floor, but it must compete with newer direct clone models rather than receive the adaptation budget by default.
nextBuild.reversal: Promote if it wins the same blind Hindi gates; remove if access, prompt transcript sensitivity, or identity fidelity blocks a fair run.

vendorAnchors.why: The most budget-aligned commercial anchor: creation in under five seconds from one minute and synthesis in more than 90 languages, including Hindi.
Stable 2026 snapshot with explicit Hindi support; professional cloning is a separate two-hour-quality anchor.
India-built anchor with explicit Hindi-English code-switching and Indian voices.
Expressive speech-language-model anchor with Hindi and short-reference cloning.

researchOnly.reason: Useful 646-language research control, but the official model card makes pretrained weights noncommercial because of training-data constraints.
Its IPA, dual language-ID, and transcript-free conditioning recipe is useful research evidence, but the released weights are noncommercial.

data.role: The only speaker-identity adaptation set. Record Hindi, spontaneous Hinglish, and Indian English separately, with held-out prompts.
Language and Indian-speaker diversity adaptation only, never a named person's identity adapter.
Held-out Indian speaker and content diagnostics after a rights audit; not the first production training corpus.
Hindi and long-audio stress test only. It cannot train a deployable named identity without the speaker's recorded permission.

evaluation.indistinguishableRule: On held-out matched text, the clustered 95 percent interval for real-versus-clone discrimination must fit inside 45 to 55 percent, catch accuracy must pass, and no critical human axis may be inferior by more than 0.2 on a five-point scale.
evaluation.winRule: Against each vendor, the clustered 95 percent lower bound of paired preference must exceed 50 percent, with owner preference reported separately.

architecture.primary: Direct multilingual clone model with explicit language tags, a language-matched reference bank, and one owner LoRA on a frozen qualified base.
architecture.referenceBank: Keep 6 to 12 clean 6-to-12-second owner windows stratified by Hindi, Hinglish, English, neutral teaching, correction, encouragement, and high-energy delivery. Select by target language and style before synthesis.
architecture.openVoiceRole: Diagnostic conversion arm only. Tone-color conversion does not preserve the full accent, articulation, rhythm, breath, or intonation needed for an exact human clone.
architecture.foundationTraining: Rejected under this budget. USD 1,000 can qualify bases and run parameter-efficient adaptation; it cannot reproduce training runs based on hundreds of thousands or millions of hours.
